title: Important, easy improvements that would go a long way
text: I remember when Duolingo actually had explanations for mistakes in lessons that felt academic. Now, it doesn’t teach basic app interface, especially with multilingual typing. It relies on a “teach once, move on”format where after it initially teaches a lesson, the mistake explanations do not help at all. Rather than explaining grammar and sentence structure, it just gives basic translation errors. Humans aren’t AI. Let us review initial lessons and return to them when we need to relearn structure and format. Not allowing this review of material makes no sense. Then with the review options that do exist, it doesn’t allow the user to select things they specifically need help on. New words aren’t counted in the mistakes tab, so the only way to review them, is to hope they are in the random word generator review, or to continue on with lessons, not knowing what the words mean. These problems are easy fixes. With more attention to the basic tools for learning, and less on the AI design, users could learn the language faster and better. Duolingo already is helping people learn more languages, but there important, easy improvements that would go a long way!

title: Testing is not teaching
text:
I’m not sure if many of you are aware of what teaching is, but don’t you take a class to learn how to take the ACT and SAT? Can I just give you the ACT or SAT and that is considered the class you take? 

If that kind of logic seems faulty; then why does Duolingo test you on the subject matter, but never teach you the subject matter. All it does is tell you when you’re wrong, explain, very poorly why you failed the question, and last I checked; that’s not how people learn things. Granted there are multiple different learning styles, but test taking is a completely separate skill from learning a language. Thus someone like me, who’s a fantastic test taker understands that when the question asks me to conjugate a sentence about someone leaving into French that the word “partir” is correct. “Sortir,” which is technically not “to leave” but translates as “to exit” is incorrect. But because of the particular lesson chapter I was in, “sortir” was the required answer and “partir”was not accepted. The program fails because it does not allow for the use of interchangeable words in syntax.

Duolingo is not a program that teaches you language, it teaches you how to take tests. It is, however, the only way I have to practice my French, so at 40 +, all I do is sit around and take French tests and that is not enough to prevent the deterioration of my skill.
